visual_alternatives.evidence: Sustained positive (eastward) displacement in the E component starting near index 580, departing from the pre-event mean of ~-1 MAD units and rising to ~+3 MAD units. The N component shows a concurrent but less pronounced upward trend during this period. After index 620, the E component plateaus at the elevated level, indicating arrest of the active movement.

Sustained displacement activity is observed starting at index 608. Prior to this onset (indices ~365-607), the station exhibited stable noise with mean N/E/U displacements near zero (N: -1.5mm, E: -0.5mm). From index 608 onwards, there is a persistent departure from this baseline: the East component shifts significantly positive (mean > +1.5mm) and the North component rises (mean > +1.5mm), while the Up component remains relatively stable but elevated compared to the pre-onset period. This coherent, long-term movement continues without arrest until the final sample at index 729.

Sustained multi-axis deformation confirmed. N component shows a clear downward trend departing from the pre-event level (~0 MAD units) to a lower plateau (~-35 MAD units). E and U components show corresponding upward trends. The movement is continuous between these bounds, distinct from the stable reference period and the post-arrest plateau.

Sustained westward motion in N (approx. +8mm to -35mm), persistent eastward drift in E (approx. 0mm to +10mm), and continuous subsidence in U (approx. -5mm to -30mm) following an initial abrupt departure from the pre-event baseline.
Sustained positive displacement in the N component and negative displacement in the U component, departing from the stable pre-546 baseline and transitioning into a plateau after index 620.

Sustained eastward displacement (~+30mm) and westward subsidence (~-8mm) initiated at index 546. The motion is persistent and monotonic in the E-axis, contrasting sharply with the pre-event noise. Activity does not arrest within the observed window, extending to the final sample at index 729.

Sustained motion begins with a clear departure from the pre-505 flat baseline, showing a gradual increase in North displacement and decrease in Up displacement. This persistent trend continues until index 577, immediately preceding a sharp step discontinuity that marks the cessation of the gradual movement.

Sudden onset of large displacement in E (-12mm jump) and U (-8mm drop) starting at index 509. The trajectory shifts rapidly over ~40 days to a new stable level, with E settling around +10mm and U around -10mm relative to the previous baseline. Activity ceases as the curve flattens into a plateau after index 548.

Resumption of sustained deformation starting at index 620. The E component trends steadily downward from ~+10mm to ~-35mm, while the U component continues to subside from ~-10mm to ~-20mm. This linear-like progression indicates continuous movement until arrest around index 670, where the curves flatten into a final plateau for the remainder of the record.

The E component shows clear, sustained positive displacement beginning around index 580, departing from the flat pre-onset trajectory. This movement continues without arrest to the end of the monitoring window (index 729). The N and U components exhibit correlated upward trends during this interval, confirming coherent deformation activity.

East axis exhibits continuous positive displacement from ~0 mm to >17 mm over the interval, departing significantly from the pre-onset baseline (~0-2 mm). This movement persists without arrest until the final sample (index 729), indicating right-censored sustained activity.
N component shows clear, continuous upward displacement starting after index 625 (departing from the flat pre-event level) and persisting through index 700.
E component mirrors the N trend with a sustained positive slope beginning around index 628 and continuing until roughly index 700.

East component displays continuous, monotonic displacement throughout the interval. North and Up components remain within noise levels until indices ~715-716, where a sudden, large-amplitude change occurs (North drops, Up rises), suggesting an acceleration or new phase of deformation that persists to the end of the available data.

Sustained movement begins with a clear departure from the prior flat trajectory in E and U components around index 495. Continuous negative trends are observed in E (westward) and U (downward), supported by a gradual southward drift in N. This persistent motion continues until ~560, distinct from the noise fluctuations seen in the preceding interval.

Sustained westward (N), southward (E), and downward (U) displacement begins at index 474, departing from the prior stable trajectory. The movement persists continuously through the end of the available record (index 729), with cumulative shifts reaching approximately -12mm in N, -6mm in E, and -8mm in U relative to the pre-onset mean.

The E component displays a clear, sustained negative trend starting at index 542, deviating sharply from the flat pre-onset reference. This downward movement continues consistently through the proposed window until index 618, where the slope flattens markedly, indicating arrest. The N component shows a corresponding but less pronounced shift during this period.

Sustained westward and southward displacement. East component trends negatively from ~0mm to -5mm range; North component trends strongly negatively from ~-5mm to -25mm range. Activity persists until the right-censored end of the record.
Sustained westward motion in the E component is clearly visible as a departure from the prior baseline, persisting for over 100 days before arresting into a stable plateau.
Continuous subsidence in the U component initiates concurrently with the E-axis motion and persists steadily through the end of the monitoring window.

Sustained westward (E-negative) and downward (U-negative) displacement begins abruptly after index 579. The East component exhibits a strong linear-like decrease from approximately 0 mm to -70 mm over the interval. The Up component follows a similar downward trend, moving from near 0 mm relative to the onset to about -9 mm. The North component shows increased scatter but lacks the coherent directional velocity of E and U. Activity persists through the final available sample.

Sustained deformation activity is clearly visible in the N and E components. The N component shows a persistent, gradual increase from ~0 to +3 MAD units starting at index 475. Simultaneously, the E component drifts downward from ~0 to -5 MAD units over the same period. This coherent, slow-motion trend distinguishes it from noise and ends abruptly just before the sharp step changes observed after index 588.

Continuous westward (N decreasing from ~2.5 to ~1.0) and southward (E decreasing from ~-2.0 to ~-4.5) displacement begins after index 600, distinct from the preceding stationary noise. This trend persists until approximately index 635.

A rapid, sustained vertical subsidence occurs, with U dropping from ~-1.0 to ~-20.0 between indices 636 and 640, followed by continued slow subsidence and stabilization at a new lower level through index 660. The horizontal components also show minor adjustments during this phase.

N: Continuous positive slope departing from baseline (~0) at 462, reaching a stable elevated level (~15-18) by 630. E: Corresponding gradual decrease from ~0 to -10 during this period. U: No sustained movement.

Continuous, accelerating displacement on all three axes. East shows strong positive drift; North shows negative drift; Up shows negative drift (subsidence). No post-arrest plateau is visible as the record ends during active motion.

E shows a sharp onset at 516 dropping from ~0 to -6 MAD units, followed by continued negative excursions (steps) near 570 and 630. U mirrors this behavior with a drop to -4 MAD units at 516 and subsequent fluctuations. N lacks a corresponding sustained trend.

Sustained deformation activity primarily in E and U axes. Onset at 516 marks departure from baseline into a deep negative excursion (E ~ -7mm, U ~ -4mm initially, evolving to E ~ -19mm, U ~ -20mm). Activity persists through complex fluctuations until index 639, where the trajectory arrests into a stable, displaced plateau (E ~ -16mm, U ~ -17mm).
E-axis shows continuous negative drift from ~0 mm to -2 mm; U-axis exhibits persistent subsidence from ~-1 mm to -4 mm; N-axis displays moderate negative movement stabilizing near -5 mm.

Sustained multi-component displacement starting at ~510. N shows a monotonic rise (~+15 MAD units), while E and U show corresponding negative excursions (~-20 and -10 MAD units respectively). Movement arrests around 570, transitioning to a stable shifted plateau.

Sustained deformation characterized by continuous eastward displacement, significant southward (negative N) movement, and steady subsidence (negative U). The onset at index 590 marks the first samples departing clearly from the preceding noisy plateau, and the movement persists without arrest until the final available sample.

Continuous sustained motion observed in E and U components starting after the initial spike recovery (~475). The E component shows a steady negative drift while U exhibits a step-like descent followed by continued subsidence. Activity persists until ~680 when both components stabilize at lower levels compared to the pre-event baseline.

Sustained westward (E decreasing from ~1.5 to -45) and southward (N decreasing from ~0 to -30) displacement following a transient offset event. The movement is continuous and distinct from the pre-event baseline and post-event plateau.

Sustained negative displacement in E (westward) and U (downward) axes. The E component drops steadily from ~0 to -45 MAD units, while U drops from ~0 to -12 MAD units. Both show a distinct break in slope at onset (~435) and a return to zero-slope plateau (~580).

Sustained multi-component displacement starting at index 402. The East component shows a dominant, continuous negative trend reaching approximately -48 mm by the end of the record. The North and Up components also exhibit consistent negative trends (-8 mm and -14 mm respectively) departing from the pre-event baseline. Activity continues until the last available sample.

N axis displays a distinct, continuous upward trend (ramp) starting at ~650, rising from ~2 MAD units to ~21 MAD units by 678. This represents sustained movement rather than an instantaneous jump. The trajectory flattens immediately after 678, marking the end of active deformation.

Sustained movement observed in N and U components starting at 583. The trajectory departs from the prior oscillatory baseline (centered near 0 mm) and establishes a persistent positive trend in N (East) and U (Up), reaching approximately +5mm N and +2mm U by index 674. This trend continues to accelerate slightly until index 689, immediately preceding a sharp discontinuity.

Sustained northward (N) and westward (E) displacement begins after a flat prefix ending near 604. The motion is continuous and persistent through to the final sample at 729, where the trend has not yet arrested.

Sustained multi-component deformation begins at index 620. E displaces negatively from ~0mm to -12mm; N displaces positively from ~0mm to +13mm; U displaces negatively from ~0mm to -10mm. Movement is continuous and monotonic in direction for all three axes until the end of the record.

Sustained westward and southward displacement with subsidence. From index 496, the trajectory departs from the pre-onset plateau (E ~ -1 to 0, N ~ 0 to 1) into a continuous negative trend in E and N components, reaching E ~ -13 and N ~ -6 by the end of the record. The U component also shows persistent negative deviation compared to the reference period.

Sustained displacement begins with a clear departure of the E component from the ~0 MAD baseline into a negative trend, mirrored by a drop in the U component. The movement is continuous and monotonic until reaching a new steady state around index 612.

Sustained displacement begins with a clear departure from the pre-event baseline. The East component shows a continuous negative trend dropping from ~0 to -5 MAD units. The Up component follows a similar downward trajectory, decreasing from ~0 to -10 MAD units. The North component also shifts negatively. The movement persists for roughly 55 days before arresting into a plateau.

Abrupt permanent step change. N shifts from ~-1 to ~-16, E from ~-20 to ~-15, U from ~2 to ~-3. Following this step, the trajectory stabilizes at these new offsets (plateau) without further significant directional drift, indicating arrest of movement after the step.
Sustained negative trend in N and U components starting ~560, continuing to the end of the record.

Sustained westward (N decreasing from ~1.5 to -24) and downward (U decreasing from ~0 to -30) displacement begins abruptly after index 627 and continues linearly without arrest until the right-censored end of the record.

Sustained negative displacement observed primarily in N and U axes. The N component shows a clear, steady decline from near-zero levels starting around index 460, reaching a minimum near index 590 before an abrupt recovery/step. The U component mirrors this behavior with a similar downward slope. The E component shows minor fluctuations but lacks the strong linear trend seen in N/U.

Sustained westward (N decreasing from ~0 to -3mm) and downward (U decreasing from ~0 to -1mm) displacement begins after index 457. The E component remains relatively stable with minor fluctuations until later stages. The trend continues steadily until index 570, just before a sharp positive jump in all components.

Following the return from the temporary offset at index 575, sustained westward (N decreasing from ~-20 to -36mm) and downward (U decreasing from ~-15 to -18mm) motion resumes. The E component also shows a consistent negative trend (decreasing from ~-3 to -14mm). This activity persists until index 690, immediately preceding a large abrupt step change at index 691.

Sustained, monotonic positive trend in the N component rising from ~0 to ~20 MAD units. The onset at 438 marks the clear departure from the pre-event stationary baseline, and the end at 597 corresponds to the visible arrest of motion before the signal stabilizes on a high-level plateau.
Continuous eastward displacement (E: ~1mm to >25mm) accompanied by gradual subsidence (U: ~0mm to -3mm), distinct from the pre-onset stability.

Sustained deformation activity is confirmed across all three axes. The East component shows a continuous upward trend departing from the baseline around index 440, while North and Up components exhibit correlated downward trends during this period. This coherent, gradual movement persists until an abrupt permanent step occurs at index 526, after which the series stabilizes on a new plateau, marking the end of the active phase.

Sustained eastward and northward displacement initiates at index 414, departing from the stationary baseline observed in indices 365-413. The movement is persistent and monotonic in trend through index 533, culminating in a sharp permanent offset that arrests the active phase.

Sustained negative displacement in the N component. The trajectory departs from the pre-event mean (~ -2 MAD units) starting around index 570, descending continuously to a new plateau level (~ -7 MAD units) established by index 600. This represents a persistent shift rather than a transient spike.
Continuous westward displacement in the East component from ~index 400 to end of record; North and Up components show noise/seasonal variation without sustained directional movement.

Sustained negative displacement in both N and E components begins at index 416, marked by a distinct departure from the prior flat trajectory. The movement continues steadily through the monitoring window until approximately index 526, where the curves flatten into a stable offset relative to the pre-event baseline.
Sustained rapid westward and southward displacement. N component drops from ~-2mm to ~-30mm; E component drops from ~-1mm to ~-12mm. Movement is continuous and directional, distinct from prior noise.
Sustained negative trend in E component from ~470 to ~560. N and U components remain relatively stable during this period before shifting abruptly at the arrest point.
Sustained westward drift initiates at ~429, accelerating into strong southward displacement from ~500 to 587, culminating in a permanent offset.
E-axis: Sustained positive displacement trend observed from ~420 to ~510, clearly deviating from the pre-onset baseline. N and U axes show no corresponding sustained movement.

Sustained positive East displacement and negative Up displacement begin at index 471, departing from the prior flat baseline. The East component increases steadily from ~0 mm to >12 mm, and the Up component drops from ~-1 mm to ~-6 mm. No plateau or arrest is observed within the monitoring window; activity is right-censored.

Sustained multi-component deformation activity is observed. The N-axis displays a persistent positive shift relative to the pre-event baseline, accompanied by simultaneous negative trends in the E and U axes. The displacement evolves continuously over this interval rather than occurring as an instantaneous step, with the trajectory flattening out near index 492.

Sustained negative drift in East and Up components begins at index 625, departing from the pre-event baseline. The displacement progresses continuously through indices 625-703, with East shifting from ~0mm to ~-4/-6mm and Up shifting from ~0mm to ~-5/-7mm. The motion arrests around index 703, establishing a plateau at these deformed values.

Sustained negative displacement in N and U axes begins at ~410, diverging from the flat pre-event reference. The E axis shows a concurrent positive excursion. The rate of change slows and stabilizes into a plateau by ~520.

Sustained westward (N) and downward (U) displacement with moderate eastward (E) motion. The N-axis shows a continuous decline from ~0 mm to ~-28 mm, while the U-axis drops from ~0 mm to ~-16 mm. This persistent trend distinguishes it from noise or temporary offsets, ending as the rates decrease and the position stabilizes.

Sustained deformation is observed across all components starting at index 503. The N component shows a clear downward trend departing from the baseline, while E and U exhibit corresponding upward and downward movements respectively. This continuous motion persists until approximately index 541, after which the trajectories flatten into a stable plateau, marking the end of the active phase.

Sustained multi-axis deformation initiated at index 486. N-axis trends positively throughout. E-axis undergoes rapid expansion followed by slow relaxation but remains significantly offset. U-axis experiences major subsidence and maintains a depressed level. Activity continues through the end of the available record.

Sustained deformation marked by simultaneous linear trends: N decreases from ~-2 to ~-10 MAD units and E increases from ~0 to ~+6 MAD units. Movement is continuous and departs clearly from the pre-onset trajectory, ending abruptly as both components flatten into stable post-event levels.

Sustained westward and northward displacement observed on original trajectory; N component shows continuous negative drift departing from baseline ~-1mm to ~-17mm, while E component shows persistent positive drift from ~0mm to ~+7mm, ending before stabilization.
Sustained positive displacement in E axis; N and U show weak corresponding trends.

Sustained deformation activity begins at index 408 with a departure from the prior stable trajectory, showing continuous westward (N decreasing to ~-3mm) and northward (E increasing to ~+3mm) movement through the middle of the record. This persistent motion continues until approximately index 620, after which a distinct permanent step occurs in the East component (jumping from ~+8mm to ~+21mm), marking the end of the gradual sustained phase.
